title: Roleset DSL, evaluation rules, and audit annotation plan for RBAC v2
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket proposes a compact, evaluable Roleset DSL and a deterministic evaluation pipeline for RBAC v2, plus the audit annotation contract that must be emitted for every authorization decision. The goal is to provide: 1) unambiguous permission resolution across hierarchical resources; 2) predictable deny/allow precedence and temporal overrides; 3) traceable evaluation output to support audits and incident analysis; and 4) clear integration points for SSO/SAML attribute mapping and admin breakglass controls.

Design goals and constraints:
- Determinism: same inputs -> same decision and trace. No hidden heuristics.
- Minimal runtime overhead: evaluation must be microsecond-weight for common checks; heavy trace encoding is optional and gated by sampling/flags.
- Expressiveness: support resource path patterns, scope labels, temporal policy (time-limited grants), and attribute-based conditions (e.g., project=="alpha").
- Backwards-compatible migration: provide mappings and compatibility layer for existing RBAC V1 roles/tokens.
- Auditability: every decision must emit a stable set of fields for logging and downstream analytics.

Roleset DSL (proposal):
- Syntax: JSON/YAML-first schema describing a roleset object with three core sections: principals (role bindings), role_definitions (capabilities), and policy_overrides. Each definition is a flat map (no executable code) with fields: id, name, resource_patterns (globs), actions (allow/deny per verb), scope_tags (list), conditions (simple equality/regex), ttl (optional), and immutable metadata.
- Example concise form (for human readers in docs):
  - role_definitions:
    - id: rs.viewer
      resource_patterns: ["/org/*/project/*"]
      actions: ["read"]
      scope_tags: ["billing-safe"]
- Binding semantics: principals map identities (user, service, group) or SAML attributes -> roleset ids, with optional constraints (tenant, environment). Bindings can be time-limited TTLs or require an activation workflow for admin/breakglass.

Evaluation rules (deterministic pipeline):
1) Resolve principal provenance: identity source (SSO/SAML, API token, internal service), attributes, group expansion.
2) Collect candidate bindings: include direct binds, group-derived, and external role-maps (SSO mapping).
3) Expand role_definitions to concrete permission tuples: (action, resource_pattern, scope_tags, source_role, ttl, condition).
4) Short-circuit checks: exact resource-action matches succeed quickly using prefix tries and a small LRU for evaluated principals.
5) Deny precedence: explicit deny entries and deny-by-default at policy-overrides take priority. Among allows, prefer the most-specific resource_pattern (longest prefix).
6) Conditional evaluation: evaluate simple conditions (equality, regex, numeric range) with a sandboxed evaluator that denies on evaluation errors.
7) Audit trace construction: build a compact trace containing resolved_roles (list), matched_permission (if any), decision, evaluation_time_ms, and trace_id. Large traces (full rule expansion) are emitted only under debug or sampled.

Resource hierarchy and scopes: practical model:
- Resource model uses a slash-delimited path: /org/{org_id}/project/{proj}/resource_type/{id}.
- Scopes are orthogonal labels that tag roles/permissions (e.g., "billing", "metrics-read"). Scopes are used by console, billing, and routing logic rather than by the core evaluation step, but must be present in permission tuples for downstream UI filters.
- Scope resolution preserves tenancy: roles can be global (org-*), tenant-scoped (/org/{org_id}/...), or project-scoped. The model supports wildcards and explicit "deny at org level" to prevent vertical privilege elevation into subresources.

Audit annotation contract (required log fields):
- trace_id: stable UUID for the authorization request.
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601.
- principal_id: canonical identifier (user:alice@redwood.com or svc:ingsvc-14).
- principal_source: SSO|API_KEY|SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
- resolved_roles: list of role ids (including inferred group roles).
- matched_permission: the permission tuple (resource_pattern, action, role_id) that granted/denied.
- decision: allow|deny|conditional-blocked.
- evaluation_profile: "fast"|"full-trace" (indicates sampling level).
- policy_version: roleset schema version used for decision.
- reason: human-readable justification (useful for UI and audits).
- request_metadata: path, action, client_ip, region.
- auth_token_id: token id or session id when available (redacted in logs according to retention policy).
Notes: all fields must be emitted in structured JSON logs. Sensitive values (email, IP) must be redaction-aware per compliance package configuration.

SSO/SAML integration: mapping model and caveats:
- We will map SAML/groups/attributes to roleset bindings using a configurable attribute-mapping table. Mapping rules are stored as role-maps in the admin console and versioned.
- Important to enforce idempotence: repeated SAML assertions must map to the same canonical principal and role set. The mapping pipeline will perform group expansion asynchronously on login to avoid long SAML handshake times.
- We must support attribute-based rules: e.g., SAML attribute "department=security" -> grant rs.audit-reader for /org/{org}/.
- Challenges: group churn can change resolved_roles between checks -> evaluation must be consistent per request and trace differences surfaced in logs.

Admin controls and breakglass:
- Breakglass tokens: short-lived, auditable admin tokens that bypass standard constraints for emergency actions. Breakglass issuance requires an approval event and is recorded with approver, TTL, and justification. Tokens must be revocable via a single-API revoke endpoint that invalidates active sessions.
- Emergency activation: some privileged roles require an "activation" step (MFA + manager approval) and are recorded as ephemeral bindings with TTL.
- Role delegation: allow limited delegation patterns (e.g., "project-admin" can delegate "deploy" privileges within a project) with delegation audit trails and automatic expiry.

Migration / rollout plan:
1) Create compatibility layer that translates existing V1 checks into the new roleset read-only mode. Ship it behind feature flag (rbac_v2_readonly).
2) Run a dry-run mode in production for 2 weeks: decisions computed with both V1 and V2 engines; emit comparison metrics and disagreement alerting.
3) Iterate: fix gaps where V2 denies more than V1 or incorrectly allows.
4) Gradually enable enforcement for low-risk endpoints, then for higher-sensitivity paths once coverage metrics are green.
5) Deprecate old role tables after 90 days of stable parity.

Observability and metrics:
- Decision latency (p50/p95/p99), cache hit ratio, resolved_roles distribution, disagreements with legacy engine, sampled full traces per 10k checks, audit log volume and retention.
- Dashboards: per-endpoint authorization failure rate, per-role usage heatmap, and breakglass issuance timeline.

Security considerations and fallbacks:
- Deny-by-default semantics and fail-closed behavior on evaluator errors.
- Rate-limited evaluation for high-cardinality principals to prevent eval storms.
- Signing of role maps and policy artifacts; automatic invalidation for compromised changes.

Acceptance criteria (must be met to close ticket):
- Roleset DSL schema documented and reviewed in design doc with examples.
- Deterministic evaluator implemented with unit tests covering precedence, wildcards, TTLs, and conditional evaluation.
- Audit annotation contract implemented and wired into structured logs for sampled production traffic.
- SSO mapping prototype (SAML attribute-to-role map) implemented and tested against at least 2 identity providers.
- Breakglass issuance and revocation endpoints implemented with audit events stored for 180 days.
- Dry-run parity tooling (comparison metrics and alerts) running in staging and can be enabled in prod.

Risks and open questions:
- How large should the evaluation trace be by default? We propose sampling 1/1000 for full traces but allow on-demand debug.
- Should scope_tags be considered in the core decision or treated as annotation only? Proposal: treat as annotation for now to simplify evaluation hotspots.
- Upstream UI expectations: console needs resolved_roles and "why" strings for each denied action — ensure the contract supports that while respecting retention.

Next steps / work items:
- Finish schema PR and get security review (assigned). PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8124 (WIP).
- Implement evaluator feature flag and dry-run telemetry (Liam).
- Wire sample audit logging to ELK and test retention policies (SRE + Compliance).
- Draft admin console mapping UX for SSO attribute maps (Product + Design).
